# hydrofabric

`hydrofabric` builds hydrologic modeling fabrics from a reference hydrographic
network. It produced the NOAA Office of Water Prediction's National Water Model
v4 hydrofabric for the [NextGen framework](https://github.com/NOAA-OWP/ngen),
covering SuperCONUS, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico / Virgin Islands.

![An example NextGen hydrofabric: reconciled flowlines (light blue), flowpaths (dark blue, weighted by drainage area), divides (grey) and nexuses (orange).](man/figures/example_hydrofabric.png)

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("NOAA-OWP/hydrofabric")
```

Requires GDAL >= 3.5, GEOS >= 3.11, PROJ >= 9, the `arrow` package for the
parquet inputs, and the [mapshaper](https://github.com/mbloch/mapshaper)
command-line tool (`npm install -g mapshaper`). The
[`hfutils`](https://github.com/NOAA-OWP/hfutils) dependency installs
automatically.

## Pipeline

A build runs in four phases: **refactor** the reference network against flow
direction and accumulation grids, **aggregate** it to distribution scale,
package it as a **NextGen** fabric, and **merge** the per-VPU products into
domains with globally unique identifiers. Every VPU must pass its invariant
checks before it is merged.

![The pipeline, from reference fabric and grids to merged domain products.](man/figures/pipeline.svg)

![Refactor: reference reaches are split and collapsed into reconciled reaches, each with its own divide.](man/figures/stage_refactor.png)

![Aggregate: reconciled reaches are combined into distribution-scale flowpaths and divides.](man/figures/stage_aggregate.png)

![NextGen: flowpaths and divides, with the nexuses that make the network routable.](man/figures/stage_nextgen.png)

The terms used here (flowpath, divide, flowline, nexus, hydrolocation, VPU) are
those of the [hydrofabric data model](https://lynker-spatial.github.io/hfdatamodel/).

## Usage

One VPU:

```r
library(hydrofabric)

run_pipeline(
  vpuid               = "01",
  reference_gpkg      = "reference.gpkg",
  hydrolocations_gpkg = "hydrolocations.gpkg",
  fdr_path            = "fdr.vrt",
  fac_path            = "fac.vrt",
  out_dir             = "out"
)
```

The product is `out/vpu_01/ngen_vpu01.gpkg`; intermediates and the invariant
record are in `out/vpu_01/work/`. Each phase is also its own function:
`refactor_fabric()`, `aggregate_fabric()`, `nextgen_fabric()` and
`merge_vpus()`. `vignette("hydrofabric")` covers national builds and parameters.

## Reproducing the NWM v4 delivery

The staged inputs come with `input_manifest.json`, which records every file's
checksum. `scripts/run_vpu.R` verifies a local copy against it, then builds and
merges every VPU:

```sh
cd <inputs>
Rscript run_vpu.R 21     # one VPU
Rscript run_vpu.R all    # every VPU, then the merge
```

## Output

Each product is a GeoPackage with `flowpaths`, `divides`, `flowlines`, `nexus`,
`network`, `hydrolocations`, `pois`, `lakes`, and the `flowpath-attributes` and
`flowline-attributes` routing tables. See `vignette("nextgen")` for the schema
and `vignette("invariants")` for the checks every product passes.

## Tests

The unit and functional tests, including the acyclic and non-dendritic network
checks, run with `testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")`. `vignette("tests")`
describes what they cover.
